findings.claim: Skipping `map.set` when an entry already exists makes correctness depend on `Object.defineProperties` mutating the exact object instance stored in the map; if that object is ever frozen/sealed, a proxy, or a copy returned by `get`, the new state is silently dropped.
findings.rationale: Previously `map.set(expect, results)` ran unconditionally, so the merged result was always written back. Now, when `current` is truthy the function mutates it and never writes back. With a plain Map/WeakMap holding the same reference this is equivalent, but the invariant is weaker: a frozen/sealed stored state object would make `defineProperties` throw, and any wrapper whose `get` returns a derived object would lose updates. Moderately confident this is fine today, but it is the main behavioral risk of the change.

findings.claim: Dropping `...Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(current)` is only a no-op because the define target is still `current` itself; the two edits are tightly coupled.
findings.rationale: Old code re-defined `current`'s own descriptors onto `current` (redundant) then overrode with `state`. New code defines only `state`'s descriptors, which is equivalent while the target remains `current`. If the target is later changed to a fresh object to avoid mutating shared state, all prior properties would be lost. Low severity, flagged as fragility rather than a present bug.

findings.claim: A falsy-but-present stored value (e.g. `null`/`0` previously placed in the map) is treated as "no entry", so `map.set` overwrites it with a fresh object rather than merging.
findings.rationale: The `|| {}` fallback semantics were preserved but are now also used as the `if (!current)` write condition, so the falsy case both discards the old value and performs a write. In practice the map should only ever hold objects, so confidence this matters is low, but `current === undefined` would be a more precise check for "entry missing".

findings.claim: If `state` contains a key that exists on `current` as a non-configurable property, `Object.defineProperties` throws a TypeError, aborting the state update mid-way with some properties already applied.
findings.rationale: Pre-existing behavior (the old code had the same hazard), but the change keeps no error handling and now also skips the write-back, so a throw leaves the map entry partially mutated. Noting it because the hunk touches exactly this call; not introduced by the diff.
